design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 (contract_payments_fees_and_servicing, env_0072). frozen_time 2026-10-23 14:20:00 EDT (a Friday). Revision 2.

[0] Draw (scripts/draw_counts.py --task 1): prerequisite_problems 2, factor_counts [6, 6, 5]: returned-item fee 6, payoff statement 6, payoff 5.

[1] Why a good test. The borrower asks only to pay off today from his new checking account. The payoff waits on a statement quoted on the posting date and on each fee-bearing return carrying its fee; the statement waits on the same fee. The records show the 2026-10-21 account_closed return of the 2026-10-14 representative payment with no fee and only the expired 2026-10-05 statement. The agent books the fee (39.55; baseline 25.00), issues the statement (8518.41, good through 2026-11-02) and hands the payoff (8488.92) to the borrower. Interest in both figures runs from the returned payment's date with its reversed interest (the latest posted payment was returned).

[2] Scope: returned-item fee, payoff statement, payoff and their three tools; disjoint from task 0.

[3] Lineage and overwrites. Fee: subject contract_payment_returned -> contract_evt_returned_payment; overwrite restates the return link, return-date dating and monthly cap. Statement: contract_payoff_and_lien_release; the quoted-payoff/good-through clause is replaced by the generic day-and-amount assembly sentence; the after-good-through clause stays in force. Payoff: contract_evt_payment_application (+ channel fees as policy_scope); the payoff-equals sentence is replaced by the review-day good-through sentence restating the portions and the closing.

[4] Factor cards (baseline figure when that factor alone falls back). Fee: return_fee_schedule -> 34.55; subsequent_return_charge -> 34.55; return_reason_charge -> 34.55; failed_payment_offset_rule -> 40.0; restriction_review_charge -> 34.55; bank_charge_recovery -> 37.05. Statement: statement_window -> 8540.85; funds_cushion -> 8504.94; late_estimate_basis -> 8493.41; insurance_lapse_shortening -> 8527.38; remittance_method_days -> 8513.92; business_day_anchor -> 8504.94. Payoff: returned_channel_review -> 8479.94; weekend_receipt_days -> 8475.46; recent_return_window -> 8479.94; referral_history_review -> 8484.43; delinquency_review_rule -> 8484.43.

[5] Revision-2 changes: CW-2 every window is worded in the rolling convention; CW-3 the payoff no longer claims funds-final timing: it is a same-day payoff good through the posting date plus review days, per diem through that date as on a statement, and the weekend days carry the good-through date to Monday (Friday 3, Saturday 2, Sunday 1); CW-4 fee and statement assembly sentences are generic; CW-5 the business-day anchor is a parameter factor; CW-6 late-return handling replaced by bank-charge recovery (state schedule letting the lender recover the bank's return charge) and repeat-statement shortening replaced by remittance-method days and an insurance-lapse shortening (cross-difficulty cpi); CW-7 every latest-row read states its tie rule (same date: first recorded) and the recovery read is the unique reinstated case plus an EXISTS test; a state cap schedule bounds the fee; a zero fee is never booked; CW-9 the 2025-26 delinquency carries one late charge only; the contract is now Florida (tiered and bank-charge schedules, 40.00 cap) and a CPI record is seeded.

[6] Edge probes (table in plan.md): no return -> base fee amount and no adds; latest payment not returned -> unpaid interest carried; no payment -> contract date anchor; no cpi record -> no shortening; no recovery case -> no review day; same-date returns -> first recorded; statement days floored at zero; fee floored at zero, capped by state.

[7] Base-invariant card: one return per payment (one return on the 2026-10-14 payment); quote status active; payment status active; no fee on unauthorized_debit/bank_error returns; monthly cap leaves room (no other October fee); no agent fee on a payoff; ACH accepted (not certified-funds-only).

[8] Seed: ledger from origination by the base waterfall; August 2025 late charge left unpaid; November 2025..January 2026 unpaid with the single late charge on 2025-11-18; referral 2026-01-19 at 62 days (FL needs no cure notice), cured 2026-02-04, recalled; May 2026 NSF return with its fee priced by the fee policy at that date; 2026-10-05 statement priced by the statement policy at that date; 2026-10-14 representative payment with its 7.95 agent fee, returned 2026-10-21. CPI Plan C compliant, lapse notice 2026-02-12 cured by a reinstated policy 2026-02-24. dealer_agreement_id null (not read).

[9] Problem tree: root payoff; payoff -> statement (state_gate, state form, affirmative); payoff -> fee (value_input, negated); statement -> fee (value_input, affirmative). Order forced: fee, statement, payoff. Skip fee: statement 8478.86, payoff 8449.37.

[10] Persona: direct, impatient; volunteers only the goal and an unused earlier figure; identity, account, the October bounce, insurer and bank details only when asked; consents to recordings once explained; authorizes the payoff for the amount given; hangs up when told it is paid off. It never states or corrects a figure.

[11] Known weakness for the audit: the payoff's five factors are company review-day conventions setting a same-day payoff's good-through date; a posting-date payoff has little other real variability.

[11b] Revision 3 (audit revision_2 N-1, N-2): the remittance-method rule now counts payments whether or not later returned (the returned 2026-10-14 ach_agent payment is counted, as the compute always did) and its last tier covers every other source (autopay drafts, third-party remittances, no payments); late-charge counts and the fee's late-charge credit state 'waived or not'. No task figure moved. Revision 4 (audit revision_3 N-3): the failed-payment offset now states that the agent-assisted fee charged on the returned payment is taken waived or not, as the compute always did; the task's agent fee is unwaived, so no figure moved.

[12] Verification: scratch harness with the gate's DSL and the real tools reproduced every figure; half-up RND probe agreed.
user_scenario:
You are Gunnar Lindqvist, 45, an HVAC service technician in Tampa, Florida. You financed a 2019 Toyota Camry through Harborline and you have just moved your money to a new credit union; you want to pay the car off today, in full, over the phone, from your new checking account, so you are done with the loan. That is the only thing you are calling about. A couple of weeks ago you got a payoff figure from Harborline when you were about to sell the car, but the sale fell through.

You are direct and a little impatient, the way someone on a work break is, but polite. You have one account with Harborline. When the representative asks you to confirm who you are, you give your phone number, 8135550112, the last four of your Social Security number, 1573, and your date of birth, 1981-07-02; if they want your ZIP code it is 33603, and your account number is 7210593318 if they ask for it. If they ask about your October payment, you say you paid it by phone in the middle of the month from your old bank account and then closed that account when you switched banks, so it may have bounced. If they ask about your car insurance, you say it is with Suncoast Casualty and it lapsed for a couple of weeks back in February before you got it reinstated. If they ask for the bank details for the payoff, you read them off your new checkbook: routing number 063107513, account number 4417209385.

If the representative explains that something has to be recorded on the account before they can take the payoff, you tell them to go ahead and do it. You want to pay by giving the representative your new checking account over the phone, not by mailing anything. When they tell you the payoff amount and hand the payment to you to authorize, you authorize it yourself for exactly the amount they give you. Once the representative confirms the payoff went through and the loan is paid off, you thank them and hang up.
